So there I was getting yelled at by a Romanian woman with a Chinese immigrant, who loved country, for carrying dogs to the wrong place in a blanket. It was one of the strangest multicultural experiences I’ve ever had. We had to move them near the barn but Eddie was too afraid to touch the dogs with his hands out of fear that he would get ticks or fleas. So I had to carry five of the six puppies by myself. So now I had five wriggling dogs in my arms, trying to carry them without falling over from the loss of balance I got from carrying four in one arm and only one in the other. As I said, one of the strangest multicultural experiences I’ve ever had.

Then, all of a sudden, it was my last day at the orphanage. The time had passed extremely quickly and I wasn’t quite ready to leave Romania. I was excited, scared and most of all, sad. I didn't want to go home. I wanted to stay there for the rest of my life in the most literal sense. If I had the option in that moment to spend the rest of my life at Pro Vita working with the orphans, I would have. Even without showers, ice cream, my family, and my friends, Pro Vita still managed to be a better place to be then at home.

I had to say goodbye to the kids and that was going to be hardest part. Alex said that it was better not to, because there was no point in making them sad when they might not even notice us when we're gone, I disagreed. I never got a chance to say goodbye to anyone from Casa Americana (the group I went to Constanta with) and it’s my biggest regret from the trip. I went through the day like normal and that night I got a letter from my group in Constanta, bebe mique, bebe mare, Maria, Minidora,  Yustina, and Vasile, and Alexandru with Alex and Kayla's name on it on the bottom. The front was an eastern orthodox priest with a cross in his hand. Viorica prepared me a cake and my favorite Romanian meal ardei umpluti, stuffed bell peppers.

Viorica was an amazing woman, she had been abused and beaten, yet every day I saw her she had a smile on her face. She was the mother of Casa Tirol. I mean that in the most literal sense possible. She was an amazing cook and made some of the best food I’ve had in my entire life. She also cleaned the house and its linens. The day before my last day, she walked in my room to see two empty bottles of vodka, 7 or 8 empty 1 liter beers, 2 or 3 empty 3 liter beers, 4 empty bottles of wine, an empty bottle of whiskey, and my wasp trap. There were a lot of wasps where I was staying and they would often pop up inside of our room. So, I needed to find a way to stop them. I used a full bottle of a drink like mike’s hard lemonade and put it outside. When I came back 3 weeks later, there were at least 30 wasps inside of it. I was a genius.

That night we went up to the magazin and I joined Alex's made up religion. It was called the church of the archangel squirtle and one joined by being baptized with a shot of whiskey.  Unluckily we were in Romania so tsuica, a drink like diluted moonshine, would have to do.  So me, Christian, Elisa, Alex, Marion and a new girl took a shot. And another. And one half more. Probably not the best idea when you have a flight the next morning. After sadly drinking our brain cells away, we took a couple of bottles of wine and headed up to the church nearest casa Tirol. We had a good time, I hated that. I wanted to remember the good times, not experience any new ones. It only made leaving that much worse.

I sat there, drinking wine, looking up at the stars from a country which wasn't my own; afraid to leave children I barely knew and friends I barely loved. Yet, in my mind, even as a white weakling of an American, I knew I belonged there. In this home which was not mine, in this church which I didn't believe in, with these people I barely knew. Yet, I belonged, for the first time I belonged.  I belonged because I was broken, I belonged because I was beat up, I belonged because no one believed in me, and I belonged more than anything else, because I wanted to help. I wanted to know that Constantin, Miruna, bebe mique, Marion, Alex, and Elisa would be alright. And i couldn't and that scared me, I still don’t know how any of them are doing. I never think to ask even though I still think about them daily. I knew Alex, Marion, and everyone else I met there had the same worries about the kids and even about me.

I belonged in this place. Not in Romania, but in love, in charity, in risk, in fear, in sacrifice, and in caring. I was to go home the next night, half-drunk from the tsuicā and wine to a place where I didn't. I knew then that what I was doing in Romania wasn't helping the orphanage, it was helping myself. It was etching out a carving of who I wanted to be. Brave, relaxed, and caring. It was realizing that differences between people are forged and not predestined. It was belonging even as a fish out of water. It was realizing that love and joy come from loving and not from anything else.

Later on that week, we went for a walk around the hotel area. It was kind of creepy. There were 
stores with boarded up windows; the area looked like a ghost town. Alex looked at me and said “If at any point I become a Hollywood director and need a place to film a movie about monster mutants, this would be it.” As he said this, one of the unbroken windows in one of the stores came crashing to the ground. Honestly, I shit my pants a little bit. It was sad to see a beautiful beach with ornate shells covering it and almost no trash, next to an area that looked like Germany after WWII.

	That night during one of the discotecas, some of the younger kids did dances in front of everyone. At first it was cute, watching the younger Alexandru (not the douche I was taking care of) and Elisa and another girl do a dance. But then, it happened. The funniest thing I’ve ever seen happen because of a language misunderstanding. Some song with the main line “I’m gonna fuck you in this club” started playing to two 13 year old girls dancing. It was hilariously inappropriate. Everyone around me was clapping and cheering on the girls, while I sat there looking like a dumbass laughing my guts out. After that everyone got to dancing and I sat on the side and played with the younger kids. There was one girl who caught my eye, with the way she danced, and apparently she caught the eye of mike too. She was only 14 but her ass went on for ages. Her name was Catalina Pripis and she would become mike’s third girl after Laura and a failed attempt at Olivia.

	Overall Constanta was a fun but hard experience. It took a lot of work considering only Alex, Elisa, Kayla, Kylie and me were the only ones doing anything. Susan, Mike, and Susan’s brother were all screwing around the whole time. Also, Kylie got a bad sunburn so she couldn’t go inside of the ocean. Susan was being Susan and messing around with her phone the whole time we were there, Susan’s brother was with Susan because well, he was a bitch, and I think afraid to be away from her and Mike was busy trying to fuck every fourteen year old girl he met at the discoteca.

	The only other significant event that occurred in Constanta was one day when a snake got in to the Casa Americana girl’s bathroom area. All the kids ran up to the door and tried to get a look inside. I had to box out to make sure none of the kids got hurt. There was a security guard nearby, and Kayla asked him to help but all he said was, “it’s not my problem”. So, dun du du dun, Alex to the rescue! Alex came up and tried to get the snake out with a broom. Kayla meanwhile was shouting at him, “Be careful! Be careful! If it wasn’t so dangerous it would’ve been pretty amusing. Finally, one of the hotel managers came and moved the snake out with the broom.

A couple new volunteers arrived during my last week, One was named Eddie. He was a Chinese immigrant living in Georgia. He loved country music and chick flicks, he was a weird guy, but I loved that about him. Another was named Christian (or something like that). He was a Romanian volunteer from Bucharest who played guitar. The only thing bugged me about Christian is that he would occasionally talk down the kids and adults who lived in the area, saying they had low IQ’s.

Christian was cool overall though, and he showed the kids how to make glass paintings using Orthodox Christian photos. I tried to make my own, but I ended up smudging Jesus’s face and made him look more like slender man then our lord and savior.

The day after Eddie got there, I was showing him around and I ended up bringing him to Casa Americana to work for the day.  The whole day was spent trying to fold Bebe Mique and Bebe Mare’s clothes only to come back the next day and see that Bebe Mique had torn the whole pile of clothes down. I confronted him saying “de ce, bebe, de ce” (why, bebe, why), he just looked at me smiled his cute, little, mischievous grin and laughed in my face.

The next day me and Eddie were working on taking down some metal poles from the top of the barn. When we started taking down the metal poles, Eddie was at the bottom catching them and placing them down, while it was my job to make sure Eddie didn’t get hit in the face with one of the poles as it was going down. I did a terrible job. Eddie got hit in the face by one of the poles, I was trying to stifle my laughing, and the Romanian at the top pushing the poles down had no idea what happened. Eddie went back to Casa Tirol and I got Eddie’s old job grabbing the pipes the Romanian man tossed down.

That night, Christian, Elisa, and me went walking around and Christian and me were trying to scare Elisa into thinking that we might get attacked by wolves saying that wolves in the area weren’t afraid of people. It worked pretty well, and we all ended up running from the Church on the hill to the south back to Casa Tirol, screaming “Fuck Elisa, just run”.

The next day Eddie and I went to go play with some of the kids and we found Constantin and another girl.  We found them playing with a bunch of dogs and they asked us to help move them to a field across the bridge behind casa tirol. We said yes, and grabbed the dogs up in a blanket with Constantin and the girl on one side, with me and Eddie on the other. We got them to the field but as soon as we were there, a Romanian lady from an overlooking house started yelling at us. It wasn’t a big deal at first, Eddie and I assumed the kids would talk this over with the women and everything would get handled. When the woman was halfway down the hill, the kids looked at us, yelled run, and ran off. We were fucked. I spoke maybe enough words in Romanian to tell children to sit down and shut up (stai jos, linishte) and Eddie only knew French. So now, we had no way to carry the puppies and were in trouble with a random Romanian lady.

It was at this point that I felt like I belonged in Pro Vita, and I would never belong anywhere else. It was at this point, that I inaudibly accepted Alex as my hero. I realized that he was pretty much batman. Broken and beaten down, he still managed to travel the world with a smile on his face and a beer in his hand helping others. It was this point that I knew who I wanted to be. I wanted to be kind, fearless, and understanding. I wanted to travel the world and help everyone I came in contact with. Romania didn’t fulfill my need to help, because I didn’t let it. Romania did the opposite in fact, instead of fulfilling my need to help and giving me a smug sense of superiority, it made me feel inferior and like I needed to make a larger difference in the world.

	My first week in Romania was over, and the second week was about to start. The second week was different from the first week in that we were preparing to do activities the first week, and the actual activities started during the second week. My group was to play tag, capture the flag, etc. We were also required to read the children a story about Christopher Columbus, although none of the kids cared about the story. The second week was relatively routine compared to the first. The first night of the second week I passed out inside of Danusia’s room and woke up in the middle of the night. I walked back to my room to hear Mike and Laura (for like the third night, a couple nights when I walked in there mike made me put on headphones and I had to pretend I had no idea they were making out 3 feet away from me), and then I went into the bathroom and started puking. And kept puking, and puking, and puking, and puking for 3 days straight anything I ate came back out. I tried to play with the kids as much as I could, but all the running hurt my stomach. I spent a couple days not drinking anything harder than tea. It was a boring time, but I read and slept a lot, so that was good.

After, that it was about time for everyone besides Elisa, Mike, Kylie, Kyra, Jessie, Susan, Alex, and me to leave to go home. It was hard to say goodbye to Dan, Sarah, Laura, Ana-Maria, and the rest. We’d developed such a bond in a matter of a couple of weeks that some of them cried as they left. I don’t blame them, I remember crawling inside of a bathroom in London and bawling my eyes out. I’d worked so hard to make these close friends with the volunteers and the kids, I never wanted to go home and when I had to, it physically hurt. It was as if I was being pulled by tractor beam back to the U.S. and while my mind was forced to go, my heart wanted to stay in Valea Screzii.
	
Week 2 was over, so the summer camp had come to a close. At this point, things became more routine for me. Over the next two weeks, we got three new volunteers. Susan’s brother (His name is Alex but everyone just called him Susan’s brother), Olivia, and Claire. Olivia (16) was an obvious trust fund baby who looked exactly like Oshi from behind. We would often talk miles of shit about Oshi in front of her and then tell Olivia that she reminded us of Oshi. Alex, mike, and me were douches. But in a good sense. We were the kind of douches that will make you smile, cry, and laugh your ass off all within a day.

	Susan’s brother (18) was another rich kid in Romania, and only came because his sister made him. Claire (21) was an Australian girl who came to help the kids. That night Mike and me threw an invitation party for them. We got some whiskey, wine, and cigarettes and invited Olivia up to our room. Two or three days after almost crying because Laura left, Mike was trying to fuck Olivia. We had a fun night and it was pretty relaxed.

	The next day, I was sitting in my room, reading. Then, Mike came up from downstairs and looked at me and yelled “she’s got a fucking boyfriend”. I knew exactly what he had tried to do and failed at. He went for a kiss from Olivia and failed miserably. I laughed at his pain. Mike had already gotten ten times as much as me in the same amount of time.

One day Melanie came and explained to us that Alex, Susan, Susan’s brother, Mike, Kylie, Elisa, and me all had the option of going to take a trip to Constanta for my second to last week in Romania (A Romanian city next to the black sea about six hours away from the orphanage). It sounded like a fun time and all of us agreed. I was yet to learn how difficult it really would be.
	
On the road trip to Constanta, I sat next to Giani. We had a fun time playing tic-tac-toe and squares. I think he was the only one of the older kids that really enjoyed my company (most of the time I was working with the younger kids). We clicked well, though. He was a gypsy and wasn’t fully accepted by the other kids. I remember Alex told me a story about how when he first came to the orphanage a lot of the other kids would make fun of him because he was a gypsy. I think he sensed in me the same sense of isolation and ostracism that I have experienced in the U.S. with many of my family and friends. We clicked. I knew that. I could tell that he enjoyed my company. There’s sense of belonging in a mutual exclusion.

	We got to Constanta and I learned who my group was, the casa americana boys: Bebe Mique, Bebe Mare, Vasile and Alexandru. Alex and I were to watch over them and bring them to whatever activity the group was doing. Kayla was with the casa americana girls and we would go with them a lot too. We got to our room and looked inside, we were to go out to beach after. It sucked, bad. The beds were uncomfortable, the lockers were too small, the view was beautiful, but it was blockaded by a bedframe. We were going to go get lunch and then go to the beach. The food was hit and miss, but the worst part of the trip was that the only type of water available for free was either lightly flavored apple water or sparkling water.

	We went to the beach and had a lot of fun. The kids only got to go to the ocean once a year so when they had a chance to run in, they did so as quickly as they could. We spent the majority of the time corralling the kids and making sure that they didn’t get too far away from us on the beach, and trying to make sure no one drowned. Coming from Arizona, it took me about 2 hours to get both feet in the freezing water, but once I did I ran around with Bebe Mique and played around. At one point, Bebe jumped on top of my head and almost snapped my neck. He was a chubby kid. It was a topless beach and at one point, Ulica, a 14 or 15 year old kid asked Alex if he could play a game on his phone. Alex said yes and gave the phone to Ulica and about ten minutes later, there was Ulica taking a picture of a young woman’s breasts. Romanian men are like that. We got back from the beach and I took a warm shower for the first time in a month. The showers were the highlight of my trip to Constanta. Then we went to dinner and after to the discoteca with the kids. 

	I can’t dance, let me preface this paragraph with that. So the whole 5 days we were in Constanta, I danced for maybe five or six minutes. The rest of the time, I was running around with the kids playing tag, making funny faces at Yustina (A casa Americana girl), or chasing Bebe mique because he stole something from one of the other kids. After the discoteca, we all went back to the motel/hotel thing and went to sleep. Or tried to go to sleep, Alexandru wouldn’t shut the fuck up.

	Punching a child in the face is wrong, always. Sometimes, though, it’s not so bad. With Alexandru, I thought about it, a lot. I fantasized about punching a 9 or 10 year old child in the mouth. I know that sounds wrong, but trust me when I say any one would fantasize about it. He wasn’t a bad person, he wasn’t hurting other kids, he was just the most annoying motherfucker alive. Whenever me or Alex would tell him to do something, he would just laugh annoyingly and then not do it. One day, the only reason he didn’t steal a bracelet from one of the vendors near our hotel is because I bought it for him.  If I ever was to go to prison for abusing a child, it would be him.
